title: Levetiracetam restores GABAergic function and network homeostasis following Vps35 deficiency in excitatory neurons
title_zh: 左乙拉西坦在兴奋性神经元中缺乏Vps35后恢复GABA能功能与网络稳态
abstract: Abstract Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRDs) remain incurable, partly due to their complex and poorly understood pathogenic mechanisms. Loss of vacuolar protein sorting-associated protein 35 (VPS35), a core component of the retromer complex, has been implicated in AD and ADRDs. While Vps35 deficiency is known to increase amyloidogenesis by regulating its cargo proteins, such as APP and BACE1, the precise mechanism by which VPS35 dysfunction leads to cognitive impairment remains elusive. While neuronal VPS35 regulates trafficking and functions of multiple synaptic membrane proteins, such as postsynaptic glutamatergic and GABAnergic receptors and pre-synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, and Levetiracetam (LEV), an antiepileptic drug that improves cognition, interacts with the SV2A, exactly how LEV enhances cognition is still a matter of debate. Methods Given the abundant expression of VPS35 in pyramidal excitatory neurons, we generated a conditional knockout mouse model with Vps35 deletion from postnatal glutamatergic excitatory neurons ( Vps35 CaMKIIα ) and characterized its phenotypes using a combination of behavioral assessments, and electrophysiological, biochemical, and immunohiotological analyses in the hippocampal CA1 region. A targeted pharmacological screen was conducted to evaluate the therapeutic potential of LEV. Results Vps35 deletion did not disrupt the gross brain development but led to progressive cognitive decline beginning at three months of age. Electrophysiological analyses revealed earlier-onset hippocampal CA1 hyperexcitability, marked by depolarized resting membrane potentials and reduced Kir 2.1 expression. However, restoring Kir 2.1 to suppress hyperexcitability failed to rescue cognitive deficits. Instead, cognitive impairment was associated with weakened GABAergic transmission and disruption of the excitatory/inhibitory balance in the Schaffer collateral–CA1 circuit. Notably, LEV treatment diminished these deficits in mutant mice. Intriguingly, LEV increased the levels of retromer component, VPS26A, and multiple pre- and postsynaptic GABAergic proteins, in addition to SV2A, all of which were reduced in Vps35 -deficient CA1 neurons. Conclusions These findings identify VPS35 in excitatory neurons as a critical factor for inhibitory synapse maintenance and network homeostasis. This study also highlights LEV as a potential therapeutic strategy for ADRDs through the preservation of GABAergic synapses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景：阿尔茨海默病（AD）及相关痴呆（ADRDs）仍无治愈方法，部分原因在于其复杂且尚未充分理解的致病机制。空泡蛋白分选相关蛋白35（VPS35）是回收体复合物的核心组分，已被认为与AD和ADRDs相关。虽然已知Vps35缺失通过调节其货物蛋白（如APP和BACE1）增加淀粉样蛋白生成，但VPS35功能障碍导致认知障碍的精确机制仍不清楚。神经元VPS35调节多种突触膜蛋白的运输和功能，包括突触后谷氨酸能和GABA能受体以及突触前囊泡蛋白SV2A；左乙拉西坦（LEV）是一种可改善认知的抗癫痫药，能与SV2A相互作用，但LEV如何增强认知仍有争议。 方法：鉴于VPS35在锥体兴奋性神经元中的高表达，我们构建了一个条件性敲除小鼠模型，在出生后将Vps35从谷氨酸能兴奋性神经元（Vps35 CaMKIIα）中删除，并通过行为评估、电生理、化学和免疫组织学分析相结合，研究其在海马CA1区的表型。我们还进行了一项靶向药理筛选，以评估LEV的治疗潜力。 结果：Vps35缺失并未破坏大脑的整体发育，但在三个月龄开始出现逐步的认知衰退。电生理分析显示海马CA1区早发性超兴奋性，表现为静息膜电位去极化和Kir 2.1表达下降。然而，恢复Kir 2.1以抑制超兴奋性并未改善认知缺陷。相反，认知障碍与GABA能传递减弱以及Schaffer支路–CA1回路中兴奋/抑制平衡失调相关。值得注意的是，LEV治疗显著减轻了突变小鼠的这些缺陷。更有趣的是，LEV提高了回收体组分VPS26A以及多种突触前后GABA能蛋白的水平，除了SV2A外，这些蛋白在Vps35缺失的CA1神经元中均被降低。 结论：这些发现表明兴奋性神经元中的VPS35是维持抑制性突触和网络稳态的关键因子。本研究还强调LEV通过保护GABA能突触，作为治疗ADRDs的潜在策略。
